name: vscode-nemerle
description: Development VS Code language support for Nemerle on .NET 10.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Syntax highlighting and editing support remain available, but the Nemerle language server is not executed until the workspace is trusted.

virtualWorkspaces.description: The development language server currently supports local files only.

semanticTokenModifiers.description: An escape sequence or a $-splice inside a string literal.

nemerle.server.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a development `Nemerle.LanguageServer.dll`. Leave empty to use the language server bundled in the extension's `server/` directory; set this only to override it with a development build (for example `dotnet-port/LspServer/bin/Release/net10.0/Nemerle.LanguageServer.dll`).

enumDescriptions: Trace LSP messages without payload details.
Trace LSP messages and payload details.
nemerle.server.trace.markdownDescription: Controls tracing in the Nemerle Language Server output channel: LSP protocol messages, and the server's own per-request lines (hover, signature help, document highlight, code actions - one per caret move), which are suppressed while this is `off`. Refusals, unexpected empty answers and failures are always logged. Takes effect immediately, without restarting the server.

nemerle.dotnet.path.markdownDescription: The `dotnet` executable used both to launch a DLL language server and to run `dotnet msbuild` project queries. Use `dotnet` for PATH lookup or an absolute executable path.

nemerle.project.markdownDescription: Explicit `.nproj` selection, as an absolute path or a path relative to the single workspace folder. Leave empty to auto-select only when exactly one project exists.

nemerle.projectConfiguration.description: MSBuild Configuration used for the project snapshot cache key and query.

nemerle.projectPlatform.description: MSBuild Platform used for the project snapshot cache key and query.

nemerle.projectTargetFramework.description: Optional TargetFramework override. Empty uses the project's evaluated TargetFramework.

scripts.test: npm run build && npm run test:unit
scripts.test:unit: tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && node --test dist-test/test/unit/manifest.test.js dist-test/test/unit/grammar.test.js dist-test/test/unit/serverLaunch.test.js dist-test/test/unit/projectDiscovery.test.js dist-test/test/unit/bundledServer.test.js
scripts.test:integration: npm run build && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && node dist-test/test/runTest.js && node dist-test/test/runUntrusted.js
scripts.test:sdk: npm run build && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && node dist-test/test/runSdk.js
scripts.test:vsix: npm run build && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && node dist-test/test/runVsix.js
scripts.package: npm run lint && npm test && npm run verify-server && npm run package:vsix
